If any risk factors provided by the user: If any risk factors provided by the user as inputs are missing, they are first imputed. Afterwards, a neural network model is used to forecast them from the user's current age to the age of 55. The forecast risk factors are fed into the Diabetes Risk Score (https://doi.org/10.2337/diacare.26.3.725), a diabetes risk prediction model closely related to the widely used FINDRISC model. The risks provided by this model are aggregated into a cumulative risk up to age 65. Another neural network is used to generate counterfactuals - hypothetical patients with minimal differences from the actual patient that result in meaningfully changed risk.

If any risk factors provided by the user as inputs are missing, they are first imputed. Afterwards, a neural network model is used to forecast them from the user's current age to the age of 55. The forecast risk factors are fed into the Healthy Heart Score model (https://doi.org/10.1161/JAHA.114.000954), a cardiovascular risk prediction model that focuses on behavioural risk factors. The risks provided by this model are aggregated into a cumulative risk up to age 65. Another neural network is used to generate counterfactuals - hypothetical patients with minimal differences from the actual patient that result in meaningfully changed risk.

If any risk factors provided by the user as inputs are missing, they are first imputed. Afterwards, a neural network model is used to forecast them from the user's current age to the age of 55. The forecast risk factors are fed into the SCORE2 model (https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehab309), which is the cardiovascular risk prediction model endorsed by the European Society of Cardiology. The risks provided by this model are aggregated into a cumulative risk up to age 65. Another neural network is used to generate counterfactuals - hypothetical patients with minimal differences from the actual patient that result in meaningfully changed risk.

tooltip.http://loinc.org/101691-4: Physical activity: Hours per week of moderate and vigorous physical activity. Vigorous activity is counted double to align with the 'intensity minutes' shown on the wearable device, and to reflect the fact that the energy expenditure during vigorous activity is roughly double.
tooltip.http://smartchange.eu/diet-hhs: Diet: Part of Healthy Heart Score, which incorporates the main dietary CVD risk factors - cereal fibre, fruits, vegetables, nuts, sugar-sweetened beverages, and red and processed meat. Negative values indicate a very poor diet, values around 0 a mediocre diet, around 5 a good diet, and the most highly scored diets reach values around 10.
tooltip.http://smartchange.eu/fitness-sp: Fitness: Final speed on shuttle run test in km/h. The subject runs between two lines 20 m apart at increasing speeds indicated by an audio signal, until they can no longer keep up. If no value is provided, the speed is estimated from the available variables with a machine-learning model. For girls, adequate values at age 6 are around 8 km/h, and they rise to around 9 km/h at age 18. For boys, these values are 8.5 and 9.5 km/h. Desirable values for both sexes at all ages are around 1 km/h higher.
tooltip.http://snomed.info/sct/77176002: Smoking: 0 = never smoker, 1 = ex-smoker, 2 = current smoker. If no value is provided, no smoking is assumed.
